projects.title: Asynchronous Federated Learning Network
projects.summary: A federated learning system that cuts what edge clients upload by syncing shallow and deep model layers on different schedules.
points: Partitions the model by state_dict prefix. The server aggregates shallow layers with weighted FedAvg every round, deep layers only every K-th.
Between deep syncs it serves a staleness-tracked cache, so off-rounds upload 898 KB instead of 141.6 MB.
Correctness is pinned by a K=1 run that has to reproduce synchronous FedAvg exactly. That check is what caught an aggregation bug mid-project.
On a 37.1M-parameter ECG CNN over 12-lead PTB-XL data, K=4 cuts client upload 74.5% with accuracy comparable to the synchronous baseline.
Accepted as a first-author paper at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026.

projects.title: Global Development Dashboard
projects.summary: A scheduled Azure pipeline that turns five incompatible international data feeds into one comparable country-level view.
points: Logic Apps triggers a Function that starts a containerized Python job in Container Instances: fetch, clean, score, aggregate, publish, in one command.
Factory-pattern fetchers absorb a paginated REST API, a ZIP archive, and a half-hour unattended crawl behind one interface with exponential backoff.
Pluggable scorers normalize 28 indicators to a 0-100 scale, rolled up through a YAML-driven taxonomy of subdomains and seven pillars.
The React frontend reads nothing but a versioned three-file JSON contract, with missing observations as explicit nulls rather than sentinel zeros.
A manifest-last atomic publish means a failed run cannot overwrite the last known-good snapshot. 216 countries, 35 years.

projects.title: westernsalesclub.ca
projects.summary: A production site for Western's first sales club, plus a CMS that lets executives manage content without a developer in the loop.
points: Every query runs client-side against a public anon key, so the entire authorization burden sits in Postgres.
SQL grants strip anon to SELECT-only as a hard ceiling, and row-level security filters rows by visibility column so drafts never leak.
A SECURITY DEFINER is_admin() is the only admin check. It reads an admins table no API role can reach, with search_path pinned against hijacking.
The client gate is a three-phase state machine that renders only a spinner until is_admin() confirms, and force-signs-out on any RPC error.
Deletes run storage-first with retry, so a partial failure orphans a file rather than a row pointing at a missing image.

projects.title: Agent-Ops Dashboard
projects.summary: A local console over a markdown knowledge base that runs my job hunt and tracks every other domain I work in.
points: Fastify API and a Next.js front end, both supervised by launchd, reachable from my phone over a private tailnet rather than the public internet.
A nightly pipeline reads a config of role criteria, locations, and salary floor, then a deterministic Python guard applies the hard filters before a model sees anything.
What survives is pulled from ATS boards, scored, and written into an applications database the UI renders as a live tracker.
Each posting that clears gets a LaTeX resume drafted from my own per-project source files, held to a line budget that enforces one page.
The API asserts a loopback bind at startup and refuses to run otherwise, and every file read goes through a realpath prefix check. 86 tests, traversal cases included.
